As shown, the dominant share of electricity consumption is attributed to sorbent regeneration, which constitutes the largest energy demand in the system. The reported regeneration energy was calculated excluding the energy recovered through preheating; therefore, if the preheat contribution is accounted for, the net regeneration energy requirement would be lower. The calculation assumes heating the sorbent bed from 15 to 100°C and maintaining the mat at this temperature for 30 min during the desorption phase.
